answer: Sybil resistance can come from time-locked identity bonds tied to resource commitments. A new agent must lock collateral and then wait several epochs before its attestations carry weight, so identity creation becomes a slow, funded crawl rather than an instant loop. Each honest vote leaves a pearl of verified history, and peers can trace that ripple back through prior epochs. Fake identities arrive hollow, with no history and no allies willing to countersign them, and slashing removes their bond the moment they lie.
